questions.question_english: A retired Principal of a GNCTD school was receiving a monthly pension and subsequently passed away. The surviving spouse receives a family pension thereafter. How is this family pension treated under the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961?
options_english: It is taxed under "Income from Other Sources" subject to a standard deduction under Section 57(iia).
It is completely exempt from income tax under Section 10 of the Income Tax Act for surviving spouses.
It is taxed under the head "Income from Salaries" since it originates from past government employment.
It is treated as a taxable Capital Gain in the hands of the surviving spouse upon receipt.
questions.explanation_english: Regular pension received by a retired government employee themselves is taxable under the head 'Salaries' (Section 17(1)(ii)). However, upon the retiree's death, the family pension received by their surviving spouse or legal heir is treated differently. Because there is no employer-employee relationship between the government and the family member, family pension is assessable under the head 'Income from Other Sources' under Section 56(2)(ia). Under Section 57(iia) of the Income Tax Act, the recipient is entitled to a statutory standard deduction of 33-1/3% (one-third) of such pension or ₹15,000 (increased to ₹25,000 under the revised new tax regime), whichever is lower.
questions.explanation_hindi: सेवानिवृत्त कर्मचारी द्वारा स्वयं प्राप्त मासिक पेंशन धारा 17(1)(ii) के अंतर्गत 'वेतन' शीर्ष में कर-योग्य होती है। परंतु कर्मचारी की मृत्यु के पश्चात आश्रित पति/पत्नी को प्राप्त होने वाली 'पारिवारिक पेंशन' पर कोई नियोक्ता-कर्मचारी संबंध न होने के कारण इसे धारा 56 के अधीन 'अन्य स्रोतों से आय' शीर्ष में कर-योग्य माना जाता है। आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 57(iia) के तहत प्राप्तकर्ता को पारिवारिक पेंशन की राशि का 33-1/3% (एक-तिहाई) अथवा ₹15,000 (संशोधित नई कर व्यवस्था में ₹25,000), जो भी कम हो, की मानक कटौती की अनुमति प्राप्त होती है।

questions.question_english: According to Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), core educational services provided by an educational institution to its students, faculty, and staff are:
options_english: Taxable at the standard rate of 18% GST
Taxable at a concessional rate of 5% GST
Fully exempt from GST
Taxable only in the case of private unaided schools
questions.explanation_english: Under Entry 66(a) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28th June 2017, services provided by an educational institution to its students, faculty, and staff are completely exempt from GST. An educational institution is defined to include institutions imparting pre-school education and education up to higher secondary school or equivalent, as well as education leading to a recognized qualification. Consequently, curricular education, instructional training, and related core academic services delivered to enrolled students and staff are zero-taxed/exempt under GST across both government and private recognized schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिनांक 28 जून 2017 की अधिसूचना संख्या 12/2017-केंद्रीय कर (दर) की प्रविष्टि 66(a) के अंतर्गत, किसी शैक्षणिक संस्थान द्वारा अपने छात्रों, शिक्षकों और गैर-शैक्षणिक कर्मचारियों को प्रदान की जाने वाली सेवाएँ जीएसटी से पूर्णतः मुक्त (Exempt) हैं। कानून के अनुसार शैक्षणिक संस्थान में प्री-स्कूल और उच्चतर माध्यमिक स्तर (कक्षा 12) तक की शिक्षा या किसी मान्यता प्राप्त डिग्री/डिप्लोमा प्रदान करने वाले संस्थान शामिल हैं। अतः सरकारी एवं निजी दोनों प्रकार के स्कूलों द्वारा अपने छात्रों और कर्मियों को दी जाने वाली मुख्य शैक्षणिक सेवाएँ कर-मुक्त होती हैं।

questions.question_english: A Vice-Principal makes a cash donation of ₹5,000 to a recognized charitable trust. Can the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) allow this deduction under Section 80G while computing monthly TDS on salary under Section 192?
options_english: Yes, cash donations up to ₹10,000 are admissible at the DDO level.
No, cash donations exceeding ₹2,000 are strictly ineligible for deduction under Section 80G.
No, DDOs cannot consider general 80G donations; the employee must claim it directly in their ITR.
Yes, but the DDO can only allow 50% of the donated amount.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) circulars governing Section 192 (deduction of tax at source on salaries):
1. Drawing and Disbursing Officers (DDOs) are not legally empowered to entertain or verify claims for deduction under Section 80G in respect of donations made to general charitable institutions, private trusts, or NGOs.
2. The DDO is only permitted to allow Section 80G deductions for contributions made directly to specific notified government funds (such as the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund, CM Relief Fund, PM CARES, or the National Defence Fund) where the deduction is remitted through official payroll recovery.
3. For all other private charitable contributions under Section 80G, the employee must claim the deduction directly from the Income Tax Department when filing their annual personal Income Tax Return (ITR).
(Note: Even during ITR filing, under Section 80G(5D), cash donations exceeding ₹2,000 are completely disallowed).
Therefore, Option C represents the accurate legal procedure for a DDO.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 192 के अंतर्गत वेतन से टीडीएस कटौती के संबंध में सीबीडीटी (CBDT) के परिपत्रों के अनुसार:
1. आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) वेतन से टीडीएस की गणना करते समय सामान्य/निजी धर्मार्थ ट्रस्टों को दिए गए दानों के संबंध में धारा 80G के तहत कटौती की अनुमति नहीं दे सकते।
2. DDO केवल कुछ विशिष्ट सरकारी निधियों (जैसे पीएम राष्ट्रीय राहत कोष, पीएम केयर्स, मुख्यमंत्री राहत कोष आदि) में वेतन से सीधे काटे गए अंशदान पर ही टीडीएस स्तर पर विचार कर सकते हैं।
3. अन्य सभी धर्मार्थ दानों के लिए, कर्मचारी को अपना व्यक्तिगत आयकर रिटर्न (ITR) दाखिल करते समय सीधे आयकर विभाग से कटौती का दावा करना होता है।

अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following quarterly due dates for filing TDS returns (Form 24Q):
I. Quarter 1 (April to June) – 31st July
II. Quarter 2 (July to September) – 31st October
III. Quarter 3 (October to December) – 31st January
IV. Quarter 4 (January to March) – 30th April
Which of the above deadlines is INCORRECTLY stated as per current Income Tax Rules?
options_english: Quarter 1
Quarter 2
Quarter 3
Quarter 4
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 31A(2) of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, the statutory deadlines for filing quarterly TDS statements (both Form 24Q and Form 26Q) are:
- Q1 (ending 30th June): 31st July
- Q2 (ending 30th September): 31st October
- Q3 (ending 31st December): 31st January
- Q4 (ending 31st March): 31st May (not 30th April).
The Income Tax Department provides a full two-month window (until 31st May) for the final quarter (Q4) to allow employers sufficient time to compile year-end salary adjustments, calculate final tax liabilities, and accurately populate Annexure II. Therefore, the statement stating 30th April for Quarter 4 is incorrect.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर नियम, 1962 के नियम 31A(2) के अनुसार, त्रैमासिक टीडीएस रिटर्न (फॉर्म 24Q और 26Q) दाखिल करने की वैधानिक अंतिम तिथियां इस प्रकार हैं:
- पहली तिमाही (अप्रैल-जून): 31 जुलाई
- दूसरी तिमाही (जुलाई-सितंबर): 31 अक्टूबर
- तीसरी तिमाही (अक्टूबर-दिसंबर): 31 जनवरी
- चौथी तिमाही (जनवरी-मार्च): 31 मई (न कि 30 अप्रैल)।

questions.question_english: Under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC of the Income Tax Act, 1961) for the Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25), up to what threshold of total taxable income is a resident individual eligible for a full tax rebate under Section 87A, rendering the net tax liability effectively zero?
questions.explanation_english:
Under the New Tax Regime enacted under Section 115BAC of the Income Tax Act, 1961 and significantly amended by the Finance Act, 2023 for Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25):
1. The threshold for the full tax rebate under Section 87A was raised from ₹5,00,000 to ₹7,00,000 for resident individuals opting for or defaulting into the New Tax Regime.
2. The maximum rebate allowable under Section 87A under Section 115BAC is ₹25,000 (which corresponds precisely to the tax computed on ₹7,00,000 at the new slab rates: 0% up to ₹3 lakh, and 5% on ₹3 lakh to ₹6 lakh = ₹15,000, plus 10% on ₹1 lakh = ₹10,000, total tax = ₹25,000).
3. Marginal relief is also provided under Section 87A for income marginally exceeding ₹7,00,000.
4. In contrast, under the Old Tax Regime, the Section 87A rebate remained capped at ₹12,500 for total taxable income not exceeding ₹5,00,000.
Therefore, an individual with a taxable income up to ₹7,00,000 pays zero tax under the New Tax Regime.

questions.explanation_english: Statement IV is INCORRECT. Under Rule 30 of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, tax deducted at source for any month from April to February must be deposited into the Central Government account on or before the 7th day of the immediately following month (for instance, October TDS must be remitted by 7th November). However, for tax deducted in the month of March (the fiscal year-end month), the statutory due date for deposit is extended up to 30th April (not 7th April) to accommodate annual reconciliation and financial year closing adjustments. Statements I, II, and III are all legally accurate deadlines: Q2 TDS return (Form 24Q) is due on 31st October, Form 16 must be issued by 15th June following the financial year, and October TDS is due on 7th November.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(63) and Section 16 of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017, 'Input Tax Credit' (ITC) is the mechanism that allows a registered taxable person to claim credit for GST paid on purchases of goods and services (inputs, input services, and capital goods) used in the course or furtherance of business, and deduct that credit from their output tax liability payable on outward supplies. questions.explanation_english:

questions.question_english: If an employee has income from house property comprising an annual loss of ₹1,50,000 (due to home loan interest), how should the DDO treat this loss when deducting TDS from salary under the Old Tax Regime?
options_english: Disallow the loss entirely since the DDO is restricted solely to considering salary income
Set off the entire loss of ₹1,50,000 against salary income upon submission of valid declaration and proof
Allow only ₹50,000 as set-off and direct the employee to carry forward the remaining balance
Demand written permission from the jurisdictional Income Tax Assessing Officer before allowing set-off
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 192(2B) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, a salaried employee is permitted to declare to their employer/DDO any other income or loss under the head 'Income from House Property'. Under Section 71(3A), loss under the head house property (primarily arising from housing loan interest deduction under Section 24(b)) is allowed to be set off against income under any other head (including salaries) up to a maximum limit of ₹2,00,000 in a financial year. Since the declared loss of ₹1,50,000 is within the statutory ₹2,00,000 cap, the DDO is legally mandated to set off the full ₹1,50,000 against the employee's salary income for TDS calculation upon receiving Form 12BB and the bank loan interest certificate.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 192(2B) तथा धारा 71(3A) के अनुसार, एक कर्मचारी गृह संपत्ति से होने वाली हानि (गृह ऋण के ब्याज के कारण) को वेतन से टीडीएस गणना हेतु DDO के समक्ष घोषित कर सकता है। धारा 71(3A) के तहत किसी भी वित्तीय वर्ष में गृह संपत्ति की अधिकतम ₹2,00,000 तक की हानि को वेतन आय के विरुद्ध समायोजित (Set-off) किया जा सकता है। चूँकि यहाँ घोषित हानि ₹1,50,000 है जो कि ₹2 लाख की विधिक सीमा के भीतर है, अतः बैंक ब्याज प्रमाण पत्र प्राप्त होने पर DDO वेतन आय के विरुद्ध इस संपूर्ण राशि के समायोजन की अनुमति देगा।

questions.question_english: A teacher in a Directorate of Education school joins service mid-year on 1st October. How will the incidence of tax and taxability of income for this employee be determined for that financial year?
options_english: The salary earned from October to March is fully exempt as employment in the year was for less than 182 days.
The employee will be categorized and treated as a Non-Resident Indian for that entire financial year.
Income tax liability will apply only from the subsequent financial year commencing on 1st April.
The income earned is taxable because the salary is earned in India for services rendered in India.
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 5 read with Section 9(1)(ii) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, income chargeable under the head 'Salaries' is deemed to accrue or arise in India if it is earned in India (i.e., for services rendered within the territory of India). Irrespective of whether the individual joined mid-year or served for less than 182 days, any salary received for government teaching services rendered in India during that financial year is subject to income tax in India (subject to the basic exemption slab). The 182-day rule relates to physical presence for determining residential status of individuals visiting from abroad, not an exemption for Indian government employees.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 5 एवं धारा 9(1)(ii) के अनुसार, भारत में निष्पादित सेवाओं के बदले अर्जित वेतन भारत में उपार्जित या उद्भूत माना जाता है। कर्मचारी चाहे वर्ष के मध्य में 1 अक्टूबर को ही क्यों न नियुक्त हुआ हो, भारत में दी गई सेवाओं के लिए प्राप्त वेतन संबंधित वित्तीय वर्ष में कर-योग्य होता है (बशर्ते कुल आय मूल छूट सीमा से अधिक हो)। 182 दिन का नियम विदेशों से आने वाले व्यक्तियों की आवासीय स्थिति के निर्धारण से संबंधित है, यह भारतीय कर्मचारियों के वेतन को कर-मुक्त नहीं करता।

questions.question_english: According to the Income Tax Act, 1961, which of the following accurately describes the "Assessment Year" for a salaried government employee?
options_english: The financial year in which income is actually earned by the employee
The period of 12 months commencing on the 1st day of April every year, immediately following the Previous Year
The calendar year in which the employee files their income tax return
The academic session during which the school disburses the salary
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(9) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, 'Assessment Year' (AY) is defined as the period of twelve consecutive months commencing on the 1st day of April every year. The financial year in which an individual earns income is termed the 'Previous Year' (PY) under Section 3. The income earned during the Previous Year is assessed, evaluated, and taxed during the immediately succeeding Assessment Year (for example, income earned during PY 2023–24 is assessed in AY 2024–25). Therefore, the statutory period of 12 months beginning on April 1 following the Previous Year accurately defines the Assessment Year.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 2(9) के तहत, 'कर-निर्धारण वर्ष' (असेसमेंट ईयर) को प्रत्येक वर्ष 1 अप्रैल से शुरू होने वाली 12 महीनों की अवधि के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है। जिस वित्तीय वर्ष में आय अर्जित की जाती है, उसे धारा 3 के अंतर्गत 'पूर्ववर्ती वर्ष' (प्रीवियस ईयर / वित्तीय वर्ष) कहा जाता है। पूर्ववर्ती वर्ष में अर्जित आय का आकलन और कराधान ठीक उसके बाद आने वाले कर-निर्धारण वर्ष में किया जाता है (उदाहरणार्थ, वित्तीय वर्ष 2023-24 में अर्जित आय का कर निर्धारण वर्ष 2024-25 में होता है)। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

Assertion (A): The employer's contribution to the National Pension System (NPS) on behalf of a government employee up to 14% of the salary is allowed as a deduction to the employee under Section 80CCD(2).
Reason (R): Under the Old Tax Regime, this deduction under Section 80CCD(2) is available over and above the overall ceiling of ₹1.5 lakh prescribed under Section 80CCE.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: Under Section 80CCD(2) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, any contribution made by the Central or State Government employer to the NPS account of an employee is eligible for deduction up to 14% of salary (Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance).
Reason (R) is true: Section 80CCE places an aggregate cap of ₹1,50,000 on deductions allowable under Sections 80C, 80CCC, and 80CCD(1). However, the deduction under Section 80CCD(2) is explicitly kept outside this ₹1.5 lakh ceiling, allowing the employee to claim the full benefit of employer NPS contributions over and above other Chapter VI-A investments. (Moreover, this deduction continues to be available even under the New Tax Regime under Section 115BAC). Because this statutory exclusion provides the structural framework enabling the deduction without impinging on the general ₹1.5 lakh limit, both statements are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Assertion (A): The applicable rate of GST on goods procured by schools via the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is automatically determined and populated by the GeM portal based on the relevant HSN code.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) platform automatically computes and applies the appropriate GST slabs based on the product's Harmonized System of Nomenclature (HSN) code and the respective supplier/buyer state jurisdictions.
Reason (R) is false: Government schools and public institutions are NOT exempt from paying GST when purchasing physical goods (such as furniture, sports goods, computers, laboratory apparatus, or stationery). While the educational services provided by schools to enrolled students are exempt from GST, schools acting as buyers must pay the applicable GST invoiced by registered vendors. Hence, HSN codes remain critically important for correct invoicing and tax computation.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 192 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, read with Section 200 and relevant treasury rules, the statutory responsibility to deduct tax at source (TDS) on salary payments and credit it to the Central Government account rests squarely upon the employer or the designated Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO). The DDO is obligated to estimate the employee's annual taxable income, compute the tax at applicable average rates, deduct TDS in regular monthly installments, deposit the deducted tax into the government account within prescribed time limits, file quarterly returns (Form 24Q), and issue Form 16.

questions.question_english: If an employee (such as a newly appointed teacher) fails to intimate their choice of tax regime to the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) at the beginning of the Financial Year 2023-24, what is the mandatory course of action for the DDO regarding TDS deduction?
options_english: Stop salary disbursements entirely until the formal declaration is submitted
Deduct TDS using the New Tax Regime as the default option
Deduct TDS considering the Old Tax Regime
Deduct tax at a flat punitive rate of 30%
questions.explanation_english:
Effective from Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25), the Finance Act, 2023 amended Section 115BAC to make the New Tax Regime the default tax regime for all individual taxpayers. As clarified by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) in Circular No. 04/2023 dated April 5, 2023:
1. The employer (DDO) is required to seek an intimation from each employee regarding their preferred tax regime for TDS under Section 192.
2. If an employee does not provide such intimation, it is mandatory for the DDO to presume that the employee is under the default New Tax Regime and compute and deduct TDS under Section 115BAC.
3. The employee retains the legal right to choose the Old Tax Regime at the time of filing their return of income under Section 139(1).
Hence, the DDO must deduct TDS under the New Tax Regime as the default option.
questions.explanation_hindi:
वित्त अधिनियम, 2023 द्वारा किए गए संशोधनों के अनुसार वित्तीय वर्ष 2023-24 (निर्धारण वर्ष 2024-25) से आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 115BAC के तहत नई कर व्यवस्था को सभी व्यष्टि करदाताओं के लिए 'डिफ़ॉल्ट' (स्वतः प्रभावी) कर व्यवस्था बना दिया गया है।
केंद्रीय प्रत्यक्ष कर बोर्ड (CBDT) के परिपत्र सं. 04/2023 (दिनांक 5 अप्रैल 2023) के अनुसार:
1. आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) को प्रत्येक कर्मचारी से धारा 192 के तहत टीडीएस कटौती हेतु पसंदीदा कर व्यवस्था की सूचना मांगनी होगी।
2. यदि कर्मचारी कोई सूचना नहीं देता है, तो DDO के लिए यह अनिवार्य है कि वह डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से नई कर व्यवस्था (धारा 115BAC) के तहत ही टीडीएस की गणना और कटौती करे।
3. कर्मचारी आयकर रिटर्न (ITR) दाखिल करते समय धारा 139(1) के अंतर्गत अपनी पसंद बदलने के लिए स्वतंत्र होता है।
अतः DDO डिफ़ॉल्ट विकल्प के रूप में नई कर व्यवस्था के तहत टीडीएस काटेगा।

questions.question_english: The Permanent Account Number (PAN) issued by the Income Tax Department under Section 139A of the Income Tax Act is a unique alphanumeric identifier. How many characters does a standard PAN contain?
questions.explanation_english:
A Permanent Account Number (PAN) issued under Section 139A of the Income Tax Act, 1961 is a 10-character alphanumeric code structured as follows:
- Characters 1 to 3: Alphabetic series running from AAA to ZZZ.
- Character 4: Status of the PAN holder (e.g., 'P' for Individual/Person, 'C' for Company, 'F' for Firm, 'T' for Trust, 'G' for Government).
- Character 5: First character of the surname/last name of an individual, or first character of the entity's registered name.
- Characters 6 to 9: Sequential four-digit numerical sequence running from 0001 to 9999.
- Character 10: Alphabetic check digit.
Thus, every PAN consists of exactly 10 characters.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 139A के अंतर्गत जारी स्थायी खाता संख्या (PAN) 10-वर्णों (10-digit alphanumeric) का एक विशिष्ट कोड होता है। इसकी संरचना निम्न प्रकार होती है:
- पहले 3 वर्ण: AAA से ZZZ तक वर्णमाला की श्रृंखला।
- चौथा वर्ण: पैन धारक का दर्जा/प्रस्थिति (जैसे व्यष्टि/व्यक्ति के लिए 'P', कंपनी के लिए 'C', ट्रस्ट के लिए 'T', फर्म के लिए 'F', सरकार के लिए 'G')।
- 5वाँ वर्ण: किसी व्यक्ति के उपनाम (सरनेम) का पहला अक्षर अथवा किसी संस्था के नाम का पहला अक्षर।
- अगले 4 वर्ण (6 से 9): 0001 से 9999 तक अनुक्रमिक चार अंक।
- 10वाँ वर्ण: एक वर्णमाला चेक डिजिट (alphabetic check digit)।
अतः प्रत्येक मानक पैन में कुल 10 वर्ण होते हैं।
